speaker: Uncle (boss of The Firm)
line: Bring Uncle a bar of soap, there's a good lad. Don't ask what it's for. It's for a mould. Of a key. Which I never mentioned.

speaker: Uncle (boss of The Firm)
line: Lovely. Smells of roses and conspiracy. You did well.

speaker: Uncle (boss of The Firm)
line: Pop this on the Crows' landing over on B wing. Put it down and walk away whistling. Don't open it. I mean it. I can see you thinking about it.

speaker: Uncle (boss of The Firm)
line: Ha! Kingy's face. Like a slapped haddock. Here's a drink for your trouble.

speaker: Uncle (boss of The Firm)
line: {target} of the Crows told the whole canteen my mum's trifle was shop-bought. Have a quiet word. Loudly. With your fists.

speaker: Uncle (boss of The Firm)
line: He'll think twice before slandering a homemade trifle. Have this, I've got loads.

speaker: Kingy (boss of The Crows)
line: Need a pool ball, bruv. Don't matter what colour. Alright it matters a bit. Not the black one, that's bad luck innit.

speaker: Kingy (boss of The Crows)
line: Peak. Absolute scenes. You are now an honorary Crow. Not really. But nearly.

speaker: Kingy (boss of The Crows)
line: The Firm are rolling in Greggs vouchers. Bring us three and we'll call it a tax. A Crows tax. A Crowtax. I came up with that. Don't steal it.

speaker: Kingy (boss of The Crows)

speaker: Kingy (boss of The Crows)

speaker: Kingy (boss of The Crows)

line: I heard that from the showers. I welled up. Here, you earned it.

speaker: Skip (boss of Red Lions)

speaker: The Accountant (boss of The Northern Mob)

speaker: The Accountant (boss of The Northern Mob)

speaker: Gang member
line: Custard creams. A whole packet. I've had a day. I've had a week. I've had a fifteen-year stretch, frankly.

speaker: Gang member
line: Oh, that's the stuff. You're a gent. A crook, but a gent.

speaker: Officer
line: I'm on a double and my feet are killing me. Keep your nose clean till {time}. No warnings, no nonsense, no 'accidents' with the mop.

speaker: Officer

line: {target} has topped the officers' fantasy league three weeks running and he's not even IN it. Find out who he's picked as captain. For security reasons.

speaker: Officer

speaker: Keith (X-ray operator)
line: Alright? Keith. I do the X-ray. Twenty-two years. Seen it all: phones in pies, a ferret in a duvet, a whole set of drums in a mattress once. Don't ask.

speaker: Keith (X-ray operator)
line: We never spoke. My eyes are terrible today. Terrible.

speaker: Keith (X-ray operator)
line: Blue raspberry? And a sausage roll? ...You know, I get this cataract on Thursdays. Today feels like a Thursday. Eleven o'clock van. I'll be very busy with my sausage roll.

speaker: Keith (X-ray operator)
line: A blue drink. The proper blue, from the vending machine in visits. And a sausage roll from the canteen. One of each. I am a man of simple tastes.

speaker: Reverend Clive Bunting (chaplain)
line: Ah! The Greggs Bandit, in my chapel! I have prayed for you, and separately for the sausage rolls. Now, a small crisis: somebody has stolen three of my hymn books. Three! I have a choir of eleven and a man called Tiny who only knows the words to Jerusalem. Bring them back and I will owe you one. A proper one.

speaker: Reverend Clive Bunting (chaplain)
line: Three Greggs vouchers from the collection plate, which I shall confess on Sunday. And a favour. If you are ever somewhere you should not be, and an officer has you by the collar, I may well remember that you were at choir practice. Once. I can lie once. Twice is a habit.

speaker: Reverend Clive Bunting (chaplain)
line: Bless you. Word on the landing is one is levelling the pool table in the games room, one is a soap dish in the showers, and one is holding up the bench press in the gym. Hymns Ancient and Modern, red covers, moustaches on all the bishops. Do not ask about the moustaches.

speaker: Reverend Clive Bunting (chaplain)
line: Any luck? The games room, the showers and the gym. If anyone asks, you are doing the Lord's work. Technically you are.

speaker: Reverend Clive Bunting (chaplain)
line: Is that...? All three! And only slightly damp. You are a wonder.

speaker: Reverend Clive Bunting (chaplain)
line: Three vouchers, as promised. And remember: choir practice. If an officer ever drags you off somewhere awkward, you were with me, singing the alto line. Once, mind. I'm a chaplain, not a solicitor.

speaker: Reverend Clive Bunting (chaplain)
line: Choir practice is still on, if you ever need it. Once.

speaker: Reverend Clive Bunting (chaplain)
line: The hymn books are back in the pews. Tiny is learning a second hymn. Miracles do happen.

line: If you're after the toilet roll, there is none. There's never any.

speaker: Prisoner

speaker: Prisoner
line: After what you have done to my lads? Not for all the sausage rolls in Grim-on-the-Moor.

speaker: Prisoner
line: Pleasure doing business. Give the word (G) on {wing} wing and my lads go up. You have two days.

speaker: Prisoner
line: {thing} Nobody kicks off without the firm that runs the landing. Pay the boss, and mind who you pay: the Firm and the Crows hate each other, and so do the Lions and the Mob.

speaker: Prisoner
line: Word is {thing}{thing} All since your little stunt.

speaker: Prisoner
line: Every time you mess about, the screws come down on all of us. Keep it up.

speaker: Prisoner
line: Mind your own.

line: The screws carry the keys on their belts. Get behind one while he's arguing about the footy.

speaker: Prisoner
line: Toothpaste in the strike plate sets like concrete. Door looks locked. It isn't. Whitening AND escaping.

speaker: Prisoner
line: Bang on your door at night like you are dying and they have to take you to healthcare. Make it a good groan. They score you.

speaker: Prisoner
line: Proper kick-off on the landing and every screw in the place comes running. Doors get left open. Kettles get left on.

speaker: Prisoner
line: Phones are taped. Never say when. Never say how. Talk about your nan. Everybody talks about their nan.

speaker: Prisoner
line: Lads used to run a red rag up the yard flagpole for their people on the road. Like semaphore, but dodgier.

speaker: Prisoner
line: Maintenance has every tool you could want. Shame it's behind a red door. Shame about a lot of things.

speaker: Prisoner
line: The vents run over everything except the cells. Except some cells... I have said too much. I always say too much.

speaker: Prisoner
line: Two sheets knotted make a rope. Bend a fork and tape it on and it is a hook. Blue Peter taught me that. Sort of.

speaker: Prisoner
line: Soap takes a key impression lovely. Melt a fork into it with a lighter. Do not do it in the canteen. Ask me how I know.

speaker: Prisoner
line: Chew soap before you fake it. Froth sells it. Tastes like a disappointing Tuesday.

speaker: Prisoner
line: Officers get bored. Bored officers want favours. Do one and they might not see you. Once.

speaker: Prisoner
line: Never trust a man who says 'with all due respect'. Or a man in maroon. Or the fish pie.

speaker: Prisoner
line: See that grille behind the table? Maintenance never put it on the list. Screws are rusted to nothing; a spoon'd turn them. Goes up into the ducts. Don't get caught in there, mind, or they'll weld it.

speaker: Prisoner
line: They've been at all the locks since you started. Keep your head down for a day or two. They forget faster than you think. They don't, actually.

speaker: Prisoner
line: What do YOU want?

speaker: Prisoner
line: Oh, it is you. Marvellous. Smashing. Go away.

speaker: Prisoner
line: You know who I am. {someone} run {wing} wing.

speaker: Prisoner
line: You lost?

speaker: Prisoner
line: You look like you want something. Everyone wants something.

speaker: Prisoner
line: Looking for something? I can get things. Not Freddos. Never ask me for Freddos.

speaker: Prisoner
line: Psst. Batteries, wire, a lighter, a screwdriver. Cash or Greggs vouchers. Mostly vouchers. Only vouchers.

speaker: Prisoner
line: Alright, {name}.

speaker: Prisoner
line: Oi oi, it's the Greggs Bandit!

speaker: Prisoner
line: Is it true you nicked a festive bake? In OCTOBER? Respect.

line: Alright?

speaker: Reverend Clive Bunting (chaplain)
line: The Lord moves in mysterious ways. So does the tea trolley.

line: Choir at four. Bring your lungs.

line: A blue drink. The proper blue, from the vending machine in visits. And a sausage roll from the canteen. {thing} of each, mind. Inflation.
